source: High Country Fly Fishing Guides and Locals

conditions.overall: Wild streams have been fishing well after recent rain, with water levels dropping but fish still active and eating well. Tailwaters on both the Watauga and South Holston are seeing all-day generation with high water flows.

tactics: The best fishing on wild streams was after the water cleared up but hadn't fallen out completely — this 'sweet spot' lasted for a couple of days.
As water levels drop, stay back from the hole you're fishing as much as possible to avoid spooking fish.
Use smaller dry flies and nymphs to avoid causing a ton of commotion on the surface as water levels drop.
Dry dropper fishing is recommended for wild creeks.
On tailwaters, follow the TVA generation schedule — when rivers return to low flow, the first day of low water can be spectacular for wade fishing.
Sulphur hatches have been occurring in droves on the Watauga in the evening — time your fishing accordingly.
Always check current dam release schedules from TVA before heading out — flows can change without notice.

waters.name: Wild Streams (Western North Carolina)
waters.note: Fishing well after recent rain; fish are still happy and eating well even as water levels have dropped back down.

waters.name: Delayed Harvest Streams (Western North Carolina)
waters.note: Delayed Harvest season ends June 6, opening to catch-and-keep. Once harvest is allowed, fishing drops off quickly. DSO recommends seeking other stream options. Next stocking will occur in October and November.

waters.name: Watauga River
waters.note: Seeing all-day generation; fishing great on high water. Sulphur hatches occurring in droves in the evening. Better conditions for drift boat anglers than wade fishermen at current flows.

waters.name: South Holston River
waters.note: Seeing all-day generation after months of low water. Reports haven't been as good as the Watauga but folks are still catching fish. High water should jump start the sulphur hatch.

elevation_note: High Country streams (Boone, 3300-4000ft) run 1-2 weeks behind lower-elevation WNC
stocking_note: Delayed Harvest streams open to catch-and-keep on June 6. The next stocking of NC Delayed Harvest streams will occur in October and November.
